speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Minister for Transport in view of the recent instance of a child being hit by a cyclist at Serangoon Park Connector, what are the measures taken to safeguard vulnerable persons on footpaths such as children and the elderly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: His parents had posted a photograph of him after the incident on social media.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Some of us would have seen the photograph.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: As a result of that, he could not eat or sleep very well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It has been about three weeks since the incident.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: I hope he has fully recovered by now.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: His parents were very sensible and mature in their handling of the matter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Even though they posted the photograph on social media and it went viral, they made it very clear that their purpose was not to denounce the cyclist but to alert other cyclists of the potential risks when they use shared pathways, such park connectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It is clear that we do not just need enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We need more education in order to further promote safe and considerate cycling.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: It is an issue that residents in Clementi, both cyclists as well as pedestrians, have raised on how to peacefully and happily co-exist and share spaces together.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would the Ministry consider mandating the use of licensed plates on bicycles to enhance accountability in the unfortunate event of accidents and also to protect cyclists from cases of mistaken identity?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is a pertinent question, whether licensing will help.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And one can imagine the benefits of doing so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With licensing, you could maintain a register and, in the event there is an accident, presumably we can trace who might have caused it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But it really depends on whether the register is regularly updated and whether the information which it contains is accurate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Years ago, I was living and working in China, and I remember buying a bicycle.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My memory is fading but I can remember having to give my name, address and, of course, I had to pay a fee.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And then I was given a small little plate to affix to my pink bike.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there was a register that said who had purchased this bike.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When I finished my posting and was packing to go home, this bicycle just would not fit.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I gave it away and, if you ask me whom I gave it to, I honestly cannot remember.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Quite frankly, whoever was maintaining that register is not any wiser.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is just one of the implementation difficulties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Members of Parliament on the ground, we have also encountered in void decks sometimes abandoned bicycles, unclaimed bicycles still chained to the bicycle racks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are at a loss as to what to do because we cannot figure out who owns it and what will happen if we just removed it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Bear in mind also that bicycles are owned by people of a very wide age range.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They use it for a few years and then the family decides to hand it down to someone else.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State whether the Ministry of Transport (MOT) would think about introducing speed limits for cycling at parks or park connectors?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Just to share that I was doing a jog at Gardens by the Bay East and I had cyclists zipping by at high speed as if they were on a racing track.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I thought it was very dangerous because there were also young children running along the park connectors.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It may be a Ministry of National Development (MND) issue because we should not really design park connectors with too-wide bicycle paths that allow bicycles to speed.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Lim, can you put the question, please?
